content:
According to reports, this fall's Apple iPhone lineup will be headlined by the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra. Here are three of the most important feature differences (excluding price) that could influence your upgrade decision.

Design: Traditional vs. Foldable

This difference is the most obvious, but it's still worth mentioning because it's also the most important.

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will continue the same basic design language that iPhones have used for years. Their display sizes and overall design are reportedly identical to the previous generation. If you prefer the traditional iPhone feel, the iPhone 18 Pro will be your top choice.

As for the iPhone Ultra, it will be Apple's first foldable model. It features a completely different body design, with an outer screen that's shorter and wider than a traditional iPhone, while the inner screen resembles an iPad mini.

Camera: Pro Will Continue to Reign Supreme

Apple has always reserved its most advanced and innovative camera technology for the Pro models. This year is no exception.

The iPhone Ultra is expected to feature roughly the same camera setup as the iPhone 18 Pro, with one major difference: it won't have a telephoto lens.

Reports indicate the iPhone Ultra will still carry the same main lens, ultrawide lens, and front-facing lens as the Pro lineup. However, the telephoto lens will remain exclusive to the Pro models, and its performance is reportedly getting a further boost this year.

Performance: Both Feature the A20 Pro Chip, but With Different Materials

Both the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra are expected to be powered by the A20 Pro chip. However, due to differences in design and materials, real-world performance may vary.

The iPhone 18 Pro will carry over the unibody aluminum chassis design from the iPhone 17 Pro, along with the same vapor chamber cooling design. Both of these changes deliver better overall performance compared to the previous generation, as the iPhone can maintain lower temperatures during heavy workloads.

As for the iPhone Ultra, it will adopt a slim titanium design similar to the iPhone Air. It may also feature a vapor chamber, though only one source has made this claim so far. That said, due to the different materials, even with the same chip, the iPhone Ultra may still fall slightly behind the iPhone 18 Pro in performance under direct sunlight or during intensive tasks.
